faq: Do you need my source code?
Not for Basic or Standard, which work from test builds on both platforms. Premium reviews code and needs read-only repository access, so we can read your structure and packages.
Will you fix what you find?
The audit is the review and the plan. Fixes can be ordered through our feature work or maintenance services, and Premium lists priced options so you can choose what to hire out.
Do you check both stores' rules?

Yes. We compare the app with Apple's App Review Guidelines and Google Play policies on privacy, permissions, payments and metadata. Each store decides for itself, so we flag risks without promising approval.
Can you audit an app that is not yet released?
Yes. Send a TestFlight invite and a Play testing link, or an Android build, and we review it the same way. It helps to catch issues before reviewers or users do.
desc:
A Flutter app audit and code review from Ecom Swift LLC shows what slows your app down, what breaks on certain phones and what could cause trouble in a store review. You get a ranked list of fixes, each with a reason and a suggested remedy.

## What is a Flutter app audit?

A Flutter app audit is a structured, written review of a working or nearly finished app. We run it on real iOS and Android devices, note every problem we find and rank those problems by how much they matter to users and to your release plans. When you share the repository, the review also covers the code itself.

The result is a decision tool. Instead of a vague feeling that the app is "a bit slow" or "messy inside", you get a list you can hand to a developer, a budget holder or an investor and say: this is what to fix first.

## Why apps need an independent review

Flutter apps grow in a particular way. A prototype turns into a product, screens get copied and adjusted, plugins pile up, and nobody has time to step back. After a while, scrolling stutters on older phones, text overflows on small screens and a plugin update quietly breaks a feature on one platform.

The people closest to the code often cannot see these patterns, because the app works well enough on their own device. A fresh pair of eyes, with a checklist and a spread of devices, finds the problems that real users meet on day one. It is much cheaper to learn about them before a launch or a big marketing push than from one-star comments afterward.

## How an audit improves your results

An audit does not change your app by itself. It improves results by pointing your limited development time at the right problems. A slow cold start, a janky list or a confusing sign-in screen costs you users in the first minutes of use, so fixing those first pays back faster than adding a new feature.

For teams with an in-house developer, the report also shortens debates. Findings come with evidence, such as frame timings, screenshots and code references, so priorities are easier to agree on. For founders with an outside developer, it is an independent check on the quality of work they paid for.

## What a thorough Flutter audit includes

- Testing of the main user flows on both iOS and Android, on different screen sizes.
- Checks for dropped frames, slow screens and heavy start-up work using Flutter's own profiling tools.
- Layout checks for small phones, large phones, text scaling and landscape use.
- An accessibility spot check: labels for screen readers, tap target size and color contrast.
- Review of how the app handles weak networks, empty states and error messages.
- Review of state management, folder structure and how business logic is separated from widgets.
- A health check of plugins and dependencies: outdated, unmaintained or duplicated packages.
- A look at test coverage and whether the analyzer reports warnings.
- A comparison against the store review rules that commonly cause rejections, such as privacy details and purchase handling.

## How we run your audit

First we agree the scope: which screens and flows matter most, and whether you will share the source code. We install a test build or read your repository, then use the app the way a new user would, writing down each issue as we go.

Next we sort the issues into a ranked list. Each entry states what happens, why it matters, how likely users are to hit it and what a fix would involve. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many screens we cover, how deep the code reading goes and how much time we spend with you on a call. The higher packages add a fix plan with options, so you can choose what to do yourself and what to hand to us.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us which flows earn you money or keep users, so we weigh them first.
- Share a build that matches what real users run, not an old debug copy.
- Give us a list of devices and OS versions your users report problems on.
- Bring the person who writes the code to the walkthrough call.
- Plan time to act on the report soon after you receive it.

**Avoid:**
- Fixing issues before the review is done, because the findings may change.
- Hiding known problems. Sharing them lets us look at root causes.
- Treating every finding as equal. The ranking exists so you can start at the top.
- Auditing only on one fast phone.
- Waiting until a rejected submission forces the review.

## Who an app audit is for

A founder who inherited an app from a previous developer and wants to know what state it is in. A product owner about to spend on marketing who wants confidence that the first minutes of use are solid. A small team preparing a first release who want an outside check on store rules, privacy answers and performance before they submit.

It also suits companies considering a rewrite or a migration, since the audit shows whether the current code is worth keeping.

## What we need from you

A test build or store link for both platforms, a short description of your users and goals, and, if you want the code reviewed, access to your repository as a collaborator or read-only user. We never need your passwords. If the app is not yet released, a TestFlight invitation and a Play internal testing link are enough. After you order, we send a short checklist and confirm the scope before we start.
